tasks.short: Receive payment or obtain credit authorization

steps.what: Verify sale total, account and payment method before initiating payment
Rekey verified sale amount into payment terminal or account-credit request
Receive payment or check credit authorization and resolve exceptions

tasks.design: Configure the retail checkout in {OTHER} to pass the verified amount and sale reference directly to its supported payment interface. Keep customer interaction, cash handling, response checking and credit exceptions with the salesperson; the integration never grants credit.
tasks.previous_blocker: A disconnected terminal or account screen may require duplicate amount entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native checkout payment interfaces may remove that rekeying.
tasks.still_hard: Declines, cash discrepancies and account authority require resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Explain payment failures and avoid releasing goods against an uncertain result.
tasks.altitude: Less amount rekeying, with unchanged payment and credit authority.

reach.learn: Reference matching and terminal response handling

evidence.claim: A native payment interface and 20-hour duplicate-entry baseline are conditional E1 design assumptions, not measured parts-retail savings.

assumptions: Boundary is salesperson payment handling; payment-provider authorization runtime is not human labour and earns no saving.

OTHER means retail checkout and payment terminal. Salesperson verifies and captures sale reference, amount, currency, payment method and account or terminal destination in s1; its full 30 hours include approval. Existing sale-record producers have already entered sale lines; this design adds no upstream fields.
Missing or mismatched fields stop automatic transfer; manual rekeying and response reconciliation fit retained s3 exception time. No account number is inferred and no credit limit is changed.
Test supported native payment configuration first. If already integrated there is no removable entry baseline and this change is unnecessary.
research_questions: Does native transfer remove rekeying without increasing payment reconciliation time?

already_counted.description: Payment request capture and exact approval
Payment receipt, authorization checks and exceptions

incremental.description: Check failed transfers and terminal configuration

approvals.approved_version: Payment request snapshot with sale reference, amount, currency, payment method and destination; any change voids approval before transmission

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 minus 3 upkeep gives net=17. High assumes real disconnected entry; low assumes only 3 hours removable. Payment-provider runtime and customer time are excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist customers with complaints and back-ordered parts

steps.what: Clarify customer complaint or back-order enquiry and capture order reference
Find order history, supplier updates and applicable service policy
Respond to complaints and explain back-order status or agreed remedy

tasks.design: Configure an order-service view in {ERP} with source links to current policies in {DOCS}. Show dated supplier statements without inventing delivery promises; the salesperson retains complaint handling and customer communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service facts are scattered across order screens and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked order views can reduce navigation and repeated searches.
tasks.still_hard: A delay may have no reliable end date and an acceptable remedy needs discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Acknowledge frustration and agree an honest next step.
tasks.altitude: Less fact gathering; customer resolution authority stays unchanged.

reach.learn: How to distinguish supplier estimates from confirmed commitments

evidence.claim: Rasa documents an Albert Heijn service assistant using fixed flows and FAQ retrieval; it supports the service-reference pattern, not parts complaint savings.
The native order-service view and proposed lookup savings are E1 design assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is salesperson enquiry clarification, lookup and response; supplier resolution and refund processing are separate tasks.

Salesperson captures customer order reference and enquiry topic in s1 at full time. Existing order-entry staff produce order lines and status; purchasing staff record supplier update text, source and update time in their unchanged workflow.

Retained s2 time includes linking records, reading source meaning and manually contacting purchasing when status is missing or stale. No structured ETA is presumed and no automated external notice is sent.
Native views precede custom code; three focal upkeep hours cover view and policy-link maintenance.
research_questions: Does a single source-linked view halve gathering without shortening complaint discussions?

already_counted.description: Fact checking and manual missing-update enquiries

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15 minus 3 upkeep gives net=12. High requires reusable order records; low assumes only 3 search hours saved. All 70 clarification and response hours remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fill customer orders and order unavailable parts

steps.what: Verify requested items and quantities against stock and capture any shortage
Pick and check stock items and prepare customer order for handover
Prepare and approve supplier orders for requested items that are unavailable

tasks.design: Reuse checked shortage lines from {ERP} in native requisition or order forms in {PROCUREMENT}. Keep availability verification, physical picking and final supplier-order approval with the salesperson.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unavailable order lines may be rekeyed into supplier orders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native requisition links can reuse exact item and quantity references.
tasks.still_hard: Stock inaccuracies, compatibility questions and supplier substitutions need resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Check the actual part and avoid substituting an apparently similar item without verification.
tasks.altitude: Less supplier-order entry; fulfilment responsibility remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Shortage verification and supplier order controls

evidence.claim: TecDoc Catalogue supports part lookup by VIN, plate or OE number; this can support identification but does not establish stock or purchasing automation.
Native shortage-line reuse and a 12.5-hour gross saving are E1 design assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary includes this salesperson's availability checks, stock picking and supplier-order entry. Shares describe an aggregate mix of stocked and shortage lines, not a requirement that every line takes both branches.

Salesperson in s1 produces order reference, item identifier, requested quantity, unit, checked available quantity, shortage quantity and check time; all capture and manual stock verification remain in 25 full hours. No free out-of-stock flag is assumed.

Existing supplier catalogue producer maintains item-to-supplier mappings, pack units and prices; no new supplier data capture is requested. Retained s3 time includes mapping, quantity, price and delivery checks and manual entry on missing mappings.

Test native requisition reuse first. Shared stock picking is owned by this task for roll-up; the telephone-order task is an alternative view of the same action for telephone sales and must not add that effort again.
unknowns: Actual shortage mix and native requisition support
research_questions: Does line reuse halve supplier-order effort after all approval and correction time?

incremental.description: Maintain line mappings and failed-reuse handling

approvals.approved_version: Final supplier order: source order, supplier, items, quantities, units, prices and delivery terms; changes void approval before release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=87.5, gross=12.5 minus 3 upkeep gives net=9.5. High requires repeat shortage lines; low assumes only 3 hours removable. Physical picking 50 and availability capture 25 remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive and fill telephone orders for parts

steps.what: Receive telephone orders and capture confirmed part, quantity and customer details
Re-enter confirmed telephone order into order processing record
Pick and check stock items and prepare customer order for handover

tasks.design: Capture telephone orders directly in a native draft-order form in {ERP} while using {TELEPHONY} for the call. Reuse those fields as the internal order record and retain customer read-back, compatibility checks and physical fulfilment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Call notes may be copied into an order screen after the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native draft orders can serve as the first capture and the final internal record.
tasks.still_hard: Spoken part descriptions and uncertain fitment require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the missing questions and read back the order before proceeding.
tasks.altitude: Post-call rekeying shrinks without removing the conversation or picking.

evidence.claim: TecDoc Catalogue can find parts from VIN, plate or OE number, supporting clarification of an identifier supplied during a call.
Direct draft-order capture and its proposed saving are E1 assumptions, not a measured telephone-order case.

assumptions: Boundary is a stocked telephone-order path; unavailable lines follow the separately modelled supplier-order task. Do not sum alternative full task baselines for the same order.

Salesperson produces customer reference, confirmed item identifier, quantity, unit and collection details in s1, with capture, identifier checks and read-back fully included in its 50 hours. No automatic speech extraction or structured address is assumed.
Missing identifiers remain drafts and require manual clarification within s1. s2 reuses exact captured fields only and neither charges nor sends an external commitment.

Native draft-order configuration comes first. Shared physical picking is owned by task 20775; for telephone orders its shared action is counted once in a roll-up, and its saving is zero in either view.
unknowns: Actual post-call rekeying and stocked-order share
research_questions: Can direct capture remove re-entry while retaining call duration and order accuracy?

already_counted.description: Call, structured capture, checks and read-back

incremental.description: Maintain call-entry form and correct failed record reuse

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 minus 2 upkeep gives net=18. High assumes paper-to-screen duplicate entry; low assumes only 2 hours removable. All call and fulfilment time remains; shared picking has no additive saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated entry and lookup may shrink, leaving customer clarification, compatibility checks and physical fulfilment central.
reach: Counter clerk: confirm orders and explain shortages
role.ambitious_version: Provide reliable parts service with one verified order record and honest explanations of availability and payment results.
